title: When to Prefer Amul Distributor Over Others for Dairy
content: Amul Distributor Thrissur should always be the primary and only source for dairy products (milk, eggs, curd). Reasons: (1) 98% on-time delivery rate — highest in the network; (2) Fixed MRP-based pricing — no price negotiation required; (3) Refrigerated vehicle delivery maintains cold chain; (4) Amul brand quality is consistent and customer-trusted; (5) No other supplier in the network supplies dairy reliably. Never split dairy orders between Amul and another supplier. For emergency dairy orders (hartal eve, low stock alerts), call Anoop Varma directly at the number on file. Amul allows same-day orders before 10 AM for next-morning delivery in Thrissur.

title: Amul Distributor Full Profile: Contact, Terms, and Limitations
content: Amul Distributor Thrissur: Contact person Anoop Varma (primary), backup contact on file. Categories: dairy only (milk, eggs, curd, butter, ghee, cheese, ice cream when seasonal). Payment terms: cash on delivery (COD) — no credit. Order cutoff: 10 AM for next-morning delivery. Minimum order: no minimum for established accounts. Refrigerated delivery: yes, dedicated Amul vehicle. On-time rate: 98%. Reliability during hartal: delivers before hartal if pre-ordered — call by 8 PM evening before. During lorry strikes: unaffected — uses Amul's own vehicles. During monsoon: 95% reliability (best of all suppliers). Price: MRP-fixed, no negotiation possible. Key limitation: dairy ONLY — cannot fulfill any non-dairy item.

title: Sri Krishna Wholesale: Best for Non-Dairy Staples with Reliability Priority
content: Sri Krishna Wholesale (Thrissur) is the recommended primary supplier for staples, snacks, beverages, cleaning, and personal care when reliability and proximity matter more than price. Their 95% on-time delivery rate is second only to Amul. Price is 3% above market average, which is a reasonable premium for reliability. Advantages: (1) Local Thrissur delivery — unaffected by inter-district road disruptions; (2) Krishna Nair is personally known to most Thrissur store owners — relationship matters; (3) Flexible minimum order quantities; (4) Will deliver even in moderate rain. Best use case: weekly staple orders, any order close to a hartal, monsoon season orders. Use Sri Krishna as the default when reliability is more important than saving 3-8%.

title: Sri Krishna Wholesale: Full Profile and Ordering Guide
content: Sri Krishna Wholesale Thrissur: Contact person Krishna Nair (owner/manager). Categories: staples (rice, flour, coconut oil), snacks, beverages, cleaning products, personal care. All categories except dairy. Payment terms: 7-day credit available for established accounts (request this explicitly if not yet set up). Order cutoff: 11 AM for same-day delivery for urgent orders; standard next-day delivery. Minimum order: Rs 1,500. Delivery vehicle: own van, local Thrissur area only. On-time rate: 95%. During monsoon: 90% reliability (drops slightly due to local flooding). During hartal: deliveries possible in morning (7-9 AM) before hartal begins if pre-arranged. Ideal for: daily orders, weekly orders, emergency non-dairy restocking. Price: 3% above Metro, worth it for reliability.

title: Metro Cash and Carry Kochi: Best for Bulk Volume and Price
content: Metro Cash & Carry Kochi offers the best combination of price (-5% vs market) and reasonable reliability (89% on-time). Best for bulk monthly orders where delivery timing is flexible. Metro has a bulk discount threshold — orders above 50 units of any item get an additional 3% off. Metro supplies all categories except dairy. Disadvantage: 89% reliability means 1 in 10 orders may be late — do not use Metro for daily or time-critical orders. Best use cases: (1) Monthly cleaning and personal care stock-up; (2) Pre-festival large orders (Onam, Christmas) placed 2 weeks in advance; (3) When Palakkad is unavailable due to rain or transport disruption. Contact: Priya Menon handles accounts.

title: Metro Cash and Carry: Full Profile and Bulk Order Strategy
content: Metro Cash & Carry Kochi: Contact person Priya Menon (account manager). Categories: all except dairy — best for cleaning products, personal care, and packaged beverages. Payment terms: net 30 days (formal invoice required). Self-pickup available (bring own vehicle). Delivery to Thrissur: uses dedicated Metro vans, not third-party lorries. On-time rate: 89%. During monsoon: 85% reliability (Kochi roads better than Palakkad). During lorry strikes: unaffected — uses own Metro vehicles. Bulk discount: 3% off for 50+ units of same item. Best for: monthly non-perishable restocking, pre-festival bulk orders. Key limitation: minimum order Rs 5,000 for delivery. Self-pickup has no minimum. Distance: 60km from Thrissur — plan 2-day lead time.

title: Palakkad Agro Traders: Price vs Risk Tradeoff
content: Palakkad Agro Traders offers the cheapest prices (-8% vs market average) for staples and spices, but with significant reliability risk. 71% on-time delivery rate means nearly 3 in 10 orders arrive late. Risk factors: (1) Palakkad-Thrissur road (NH 544) floods frequently during monsoon June-August; (2) Transport strikes affect Palakkad lorry routes first; (3) Suresh Kumar has been known to prioritize larger customers over smaller stores during peak demand periods. Recommended use: only for non-time-sensitive staples and spices during dry season (November-February) when weather risk is low. Never use Palakkad Agro for: pre-hartal orders, pre-festival orders, monsoon season orders, or any order where late delivery would cause a stockout.

title: Palakkad Agro Traders: Full Profile and When to Use
content: Palakkad Agro Traders: Contact person Suresh Kumar. Location: Palakkad city (80km from Thrissur). Categories: staples (rice, coconut oil, flour, dal), spices (all types). Payment terms: cash or NEFT before delivery. Lead time: 2-3 days. On-time rate: 71% overall, drops to 45-50% during monsoon (June-August) and lorry strikes. Price advantage: -8% vs market average — best price for rice and spices. When to use: dry season (November-February) for large monthly staple and spice orders. When NOT to use: any time with rain forecast, during hartals, within 5 days of any festival, during any transport disruption. Specific vulnerability: NH 544 (Palakkad-Thrissur road) floods during heavy rain — check weather before placing order. Alternative on Palakkad failure: Sri Krishna Wholesale.

title: Supplier Scoring for Mixed Orders: Weighted Decision Logic
content: When multiple items need to be ordered, consolidate orders to minimize supplier complexity. Rule 1: Group all dairy with Amul — never split. Rule 2: If both staples and spices are needed and rain is not forecast, consider Palakkad Agro for cost savings, but place the order 4 days in advance to absorb potential delays. Rule 3: For weekly orders with both staples and snacks, prefer Sri Krishna over Metro for same-day flexibility. Rule 4: During Onam/festival season, use Sri Krishna as primary (reliability) and Metro as secondary (price/bulk). Rule 5: Never have fewer than 2 active suppliers for any category — single-supplier risk is too high for a small store. The composite score formula (Price 50%, Reliability 30%, Regional 20%) correctly captures this logic.

title: Negotiating with Suppliers: Kerala Context
content: Kerala kirana supplier relationships are built on personal trust and consistency. Tips: (1) Pay Sri Krishna Wholesale and Amul on time — they give priority to stores with clean payment history; (2) Palakkad Agro Traders responds well to advance cash payment — can negotiate an extra 2-3% off; (3) Metro Cash & Carry requires a formal purchase order — keep your account documents current; (4) All suppliers appreciate consistency — do not ghost a supplier for 2 weeks and then place a large emergency order; (5) Festival season pre-orders (placed 3 weeks early) often get better prices and guaranteed allocation from Sri Krishna and Metro. WhatsApp is the preferred communication channel for all 4 suppliers in the RetailWise network.

title: Reading Supplier Delivery History: Red Flags and Green Flags
content: Green flags in a supplier's delivery history: (1) On-time rate consistently above 90% over 90 days; (2) Quantity received matches quantity ordered (no short-delivery); (3) No complaint entries in the last 60 days; (4) Average rating of 4 or above. Red flags: (1) On-time rate below 75% — investigate before placing critical orders; (2) Multiple 'Short delivery' complaints — supplier may be over-committed; (3) Rating of 2 or below on multiple recent deliveries — escalate to supplier relationship manager; (4) Pattern of late deliveries on rainy days — indicates transport dependency risk. For Palakkad Agro Traders specifically: a drop in on-time rate below 60% during June-August is expected and acceptable — switch to Sri Krishna during this period.

title: Seasonal Supplier Strategy: Month-by-Month
content: January-February: Stable dry season. Use Palakkad for price advantage on staples. All suppliers reliable. March-April: Pre-summer, Vishu season. Switch to Sri Krishna for festival reliability. Metro for Vishu bulk. May: Hot summer, heavy beverage demand. All suppliers normal. June-August: Monsoon. Avoid Palakkad entirely. Use only Sri Krishna and Metro. September: Post-monsoon recovery. Palakkad gradually returns to reliability. October-November: Dry season again. Onam/Diwali season. Sri Krishna primary for festivals. December: Christmas season. Metro for bulk Christmas stock. Sri Krishna for daily reliability. Key principle: the lower the seasonal risk, the more you can use the cheaper Palakkad supplier for savings.

title: WhatsApp Ordering Protocol with Suppliers
content: All 4 suppliers in the RetailWise network accept orders via WhatsApp. Best practices: (1) Send order as a clear numbered list with item name, quantity, and unit — never send a voice note for orders; (2) Always ask for delivery confirmation by return message; (3) Send payment proof (screenshot of NEFT/UPI) immediately after transfer; (4) For emergency orders, always call first, then follow up with WhatsApp confirmation; (5) Save all supplier WhatsApp chats — they are your delivery record and dispute resolution evidence; (6) Maintain a separate WhatsApp group or label for each supplier. Response time expectations: Amul responds within 30 minutes to 2 hours. Sri Krishna: 1-3 hours. Metro: may take 4-6 hours for non-urgent queries. Palakkad Agro: 2-4 hours, often slower in afternoons.

title: Managing Supplier Payments and Credit
content: Payment management is as important as order management. Guidelines: (1) Amul: always COD (cash or UPI on delivery) — keep daily float ready; (2) Sri Krishna: request 7-day credit if not already set up — this significantly helps cash flow; (3) Metro: 30-day credit on formal account — best for cash flow management on large orders; (4) Palakkad Agro: pay before delivery (NEFT) — they do not extend credit to small stores. Best practice: schedule weekly payment reviews every Monday morning. Paying on time prevents being deprioritized during peak festival demand when suppliers ration stock to credit-clean customers. Never mix personal and business funds in supplier payments — this creates accounting confusion and damages supplier trust.

title: New Supplier Evaluation Criteria for Kerala Kirana
content: When evaluating a new supplier approach, assess on these criteria: (1) Coverage area: does their delivery vehicle cover Thrissur? Suppliers based in Ernakulam or Kottayam may not be worth the logistics complexity. (2) Cold chain: for any perishable supplier, verify they have refrigerated vehicles — not just ice boxes. (3) Category focus: generalist suppliers (who sell everything) often have worse reliability than specialists. (4) Minimum order: must be compatible with your weekly order volumes. (5) Credit terms: COD-only for a new supplier is acceptable for 3 months, then negotiate credit. (6) Trial order first: place a test order worth Rs 2,000-3,000 to evaluate reliability before committing a major order. (7) Ask for references from 2 other Thrissur store owners they serve.
